name: LIDA
summary: A British laser-interferometric axion dark-matter experiment using the polarization response to the Galactic axion field.
detection_principle: A high-finesse vacuum optical cavity enhances axion-induced linear-polarization rotation, with quantum-enhanced interferometry reading out weak modulation.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2023 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: First results of the Laser-Interferometric Detector for Axions (LIDA)

collaboration.name: LIDA Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: The first report gives a peak coupling sensitivity of 1.51×10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹ (95% CL), without claiming discovery.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
